clue.text: The bottom end for one that loses an action

definitions.text: The bottom end for one that loses an action

parts.words: The bottom end for one that loses an action
parts.note: a fighting vessel beaten in a sea battle ends up on the sea bed, so its end is literally at the bottom

explanation.surface: Someone defeated in a lawsuit ends up at the bottom of the heap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Action' reads as a court case, but here it is a naval engagement, and 'bottom' is the sea floor where the loser sinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval fighting vessel that loses a battle is sunk, ending its days on the sea floor.

clue.text: Stop dog with these-give us time!

definitions.text: Stop dog with these-give us time!

parts.words: Stop dog with these-give us time!
parts.note: put the plural timepieces after stop and dog to get stop-timers and the short shipboard duty periods, all of which mark time

explanation.surface: A plea to halt a dog so that everyone can have a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Stop and dog each combine with the answer: a stopwatch times a race, and dog watches are the two short evening shifts at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Timepieces worn on the wrist tell us the time, and they also complete stop- and dog- compounds.

clue.text: Cotton on to them

parts.note: sewing thread is wound onto spools, so cotton literally goes on to them

explanation.surface: Someone urging us to grasp what they are up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cotton on' looks like the idiom for understanding; read literally, cotton thread is wound on spools.
explanation.definitionFit: Spools that sewing thread is wound onto are called cotton reels in Britain.

clue.text: Not easily moved to do so?

definitions.text: Not easily moved to do so?

parts.words: Not easily moved to do so?
parts.note: a heavy object that resists moving needs a great lift or pull, which is exactly what this verb means

explanation.surface: Asking whether a stoic person is unlikely to be stirred to act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not easily moved' suggests an unemotional person, but it describes a heavy load that must be hauled with effort.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift or haul with great effort is what you must do to shift something weighty.

clue.text: Keeps your face from light coloured cover, usually

definitions.text: Keeps your face from light coloured cover, usually

parts.words: Keeps your face from light coloured cover, usually
parts.note: a sunshade shields the face from sunlight and is typically made of pale fabric

explanation.surface: Something that hides your face from a pale-coloured covering.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'light coloured cover' as one idea and it is baffling; split it as 'from light' plus 'coloured cover, usually' and it is a sunshade.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunshade is a light umbrella carried to shield the face from strong sunshine.

clue.text: For a long time it's been made valuable, perhaps

definitions.text: For a long time it's been made valuable, perhaps

parts.words: For a long time it's been made valuable, perhaps
parts.note: an old piece of furniture or art gains value through its great age

explanation.surface: Something that has slowly been made precious over many years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's been made' hints at manufacture: the object was made long ago, and age has made it valuable.
explanation.definitionFit: Collectable old objects, often a century or more in age, are prized for their age.

clue.text: Pretended it was taken for granted

definitions.meaning: feigned, as with a false name or air

explanation.surface: Someone faked it, and it was simply presupposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a false identity is put on, and a premise is supposed true without proof.

clue.text: On them, people play Elgar's "Tin" variations

indicators.note: a set of variations rearranges a theme, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the composer's name with its S counted as a letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Musicians perform variations by the composer Elgar on a piece called Tin.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgar wrote the famous Enigma Variations, which makes 'variations' look musical rather than an anagram signal on ELGARS TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Percussionists play three-sided metal instruments struck with a beater, so people play on them.

clue.text: They lift one off the ground four feet

definitions.text: They lift one off the ground four feet

parts.words: They lift one off the ground four feet
parts.note: an animal walking on four legs stands on four feet that hold its body clear of the ground

explanation.surface: Things that hoist a person four feet into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Four feet' reads as a height, but it is the number of feet an animal stands on.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-footed animal, such as a horse or dog, has four feet keeping it off the ground.

clue.text: Jewel the French dream about

indicators.note: about means moved around, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: le is the French word for the
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gem that the French fantasise about.
explanation.definitionFit: A green precious stone is a classic example of a jewel.

clue.text: Ruth uses a silly sort of dictionary

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters are behaving foolishly, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Ruth relies on a daft kind of reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: A word-finder organised by meaning is a reference book of synonyms, a kind of dictionary.

clue.text: Something stupid is like a concertina needed inside

indicators.note: inside means the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something foolish resembles a squeezebox that must be filled.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly and empty-headed; used as a noun it means something empty or senseless.

clue.text: She makes do!

parts.note: a do is a party, and the woman who gives a party makes the do

explanation.surface: A woman who copes with whatever she has.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes do' looks like the idiom for managing with little; a 'do' is British slang for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who entertains guests at a party is its giver, the one who makes the do.

clue.text: One with the wisdom to be worshipped by the Romans

definitions.text: One with the wisdom to be worshipped by the Romans

parts.words: One with the wisdom to be worshipped by the Romans
parts.note: the Roman goddess of wisdom was worshipped by the Romans

explanation.surface: Someone wise enough that the Romans would adore them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman goddess of wisdom, matching the Greek Athena, was worshipped in Rome.

clue.text: Pilots must be when enemy is seen to have encoded messages

definitions.text: Pilots must be when enemy is seen
definitions.meaning: fighter pilots take off in a hurry when an enemy aircraft is sighted
jumbled so as to be unreadable, as with secret radio messages

explanation.surface: Airmen must react when the enemy sends secret signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: fighter crews are rushed airborne, and transmissions are jumbled to keep them secret.

clue.text: Very bad fellow

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Very bad fellow (9)', cannot give RECKONING: the clue and answer are mismatched in the source

clue.text: Tough leaders whose men don't want discipline

definitions.text: Tough leaders whose men don't want discipline

parts.words: Tough leaders whose men don't want discipline
parts.note: strict disciplinarians impose order, so their men have no lack of discipline

explanation.surface: Hard commanders whose troops resist being disciplined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't want' looks like 'don't wish for', but it means 'don't lack': the strict leader's men are never short of discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict disciplinarians who demand total obedience are named after a French drillmaster.

clue.text: Stretched one's legs, running!

parts.note: to run with long easy strides is to stretch the legs while moving

explanation.surface: Someone took a jog to stretch their legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ran with long, bounding strides, as a wolf or a relaxed runner does.

clue.text: Dog not out to bring it on himself

parts.note: in cricket, a batsman who is not out is still in
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A mutt refuses to go out and so brings trouble on himself.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring a penalty or cost upon oneself, as one does with debts or blame.

clue.text: Statement by model that she's ready laid a burden on one

definitions.text: Statement by model that she's ready
definitions.meaning: a model in position would say ...
placed a load or duty upon someone

explanation.surface: A model announces she is ready, then dumps a heavy load on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the answer split as I'M POSED, what a model says once in position.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a sitter's 'I'm posed', and a duty forced upon someone.

clue.text: Be partial to fresh steak and large piece of bacon cut up

indicators.note: fresh means newly made, so these letters are formed afresh in a new order
cut up means chopped about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a side of bacon is a large piece cut from one side of the pig

explanation.surface: Enjoy fresh steak along with chopped bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges STEAK into TAKES; 'cut up' rearranges SIDE into IDES.
explanation.definitionFit: To support one party in a dispute is to show partiality towards them.

clue.text: Locks wooden things in a ship

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: trees are the woody plants timber comes from
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: Fastenings made of wood found aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Long locks of hair are flowing tresses.

clue.text: Bootless doing it to get toes hurt

definitions.text: Bootless doing it to get toes hurt

parts.words: Bootless doing it to get toes hurt
parts.note: striking out with the foot while unshod is a sure way to injure the toes

explanation.surface: A futile attempt that only bruises your feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bootless' looks like the old word for futile; here it means wearing no boots.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking with the foot while barefoot hurts the toes.

clue.text: Beseech

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Beseech (7)', cannot give SOLVERS: the clue and answer are mismatched in the source

clue.text: Face the side!

parts.note: a side view of a face is its outline seen from one side

explanation.surface: An order to turn and look sideways.
explanation.definitionFit: A side-on outline of a face, as on a coin, is a side view.

clue.text: Where to find the government money

definitions.meaning: the chief city of a country, seat of its government

explanation.surface: Asking where the government's funds are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a seat of government city, and wealth used for investment.

clue.text: Goes frst

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Goes frst (5)', cannot give PASTA: the clue and answer are mismatched in the source

clue.text: Fly without an engine

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Fly without an engine (5)', cannot give TRACE: the clue and answer are mismatched in the source

clue.text: Column at the back of a book?

definitions.meaning: the backbone is the spinal column
the bound edge of a book that shows its title on a shelf

explanation.surface: A newspaper column printed on the rear of a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the backbone is the spinal column, and a book's bound edge.

clue.text: Vessel must be seen in order to describe it thus

definitions.text: Vessel must be seen in order to describe it thus

parts.words: Vessel must be seen in order to describe it thus
parts.note: a vessel kept in good order is described as neat and tidy in nautical style

explanation.surface: A ship has to be inspected before anyone can describe it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In order' looks like 'so as to', but it means tidy: a vessel seen in good order is described by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat and in good order, as a well-kept vessel should be.

clue.text: Make short work of writers in such periodicals

definitions.text: Make short work of writers in such periodicals

parts.words: Make short work of writers in such periodicals
parts.note: magazines that condense writers' work into short abridgements

explanation.surface: Magazines that dispose of authors swiftly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make short work of' suggests demolishing; here it means abridging.
explanation.definitionFit: Condensed periodicals, like the Reader's version, reprint shortened articles.

clue.text: They make fine food rough on the outside

definitions.text: They make fine food rough on the outside

parts.words: They make fine food rough on the outside
parts.note: kitchen tools with rough outer surfaces shred cheese and vegetables into fine pieces

explanation.surface: Cooks who ruin good dishes by burning the crust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine food' reads as gourmet cooking; 'fine' means finely shredded, done by a tool that is rough on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchen shredding tools have rough perforated surfaces that turn food into fine pieces.
